headline: SILVER BREAKS 3-MONTH LOW — US Retaliates After Iran Downs Apache; Gold Tests $4,260 as May CPI Lands Today
snippet: Silver fell to $64.62 per ounce on June 10 — its lowest since March 23 — after U.S. Central Command launched retaliatory strikes on Iran following Iran's downing of a U.S. Army Apache helicopter near the Strait of Hormuz, sending Brent crude back above $95/barrel and reigniting inflation fears that compound already-elevated rate-hike pricing. Gold retreated to $4,260 in Tuesday's slide and extended losses into Wednesday morning; both metals are now down 10% and 24% respectively over the past month. The May CPI print (consensus 4.2% year-over-year, the highest since 2023) due at 8:30 a.m. ET today is the decisive near-term pivot — a hot reading would push December rate-hike odds above 70% and accelerate selling across mining equities.

headline: G2 GUYANA DEAL LOCKS IN — Glass Lewis Joins ISS in Recommending FOR; $2.2B G Mining Merger Vote This Friday
snippet: Glass Lewis & Co. became the second major independent proxy advisory firm to recommend G2 Goldfields shareholders vote FOR the $2.2 billion arrangement with G Mining Ventures Corp. (TSX: GMIN) on June 9, following ISS's identical recommendation on June 4 — leaving both institutional proxy machines firmly behind a deal that consolidates two adjacent Guyana gold projects (G2's Oko-Ghanie and GMIN's adjacent, fully-permitted Oko West) into what the companies call one of the largest, lowest-cost gold operations in the Americas. The proxy voting deadline is Friday June 12 at 10:00 a.m. Toronto time, with the shareholder meeting set for June 16; the back-to-back proxy endorsements sharply reduce the risk of a failed vote.

headline: OROSUR REWRITES APTA — 229.7m at 0.88 g/t Au Opens Three New Zones; Colombia Gold System Larger Than 39,000m History Suggested
snippet: Orosur Mining Inc. (TSX-V: OMI; AIM: OMI) announced June 9 that hole MAP-106A at the APTA prospect within its Anzá Project in Antioquia, Colombia returned 229.7 metres grading 0.88 g/t Au from surface — including 59.2 metres at 2.15 g/t Au and a high-grade interval of 7.65 metres at 7.07 g/t Au — the first drill result to confirm a new geological model where gold is controlled by silicified sediments bound by the Aragon fault zone. Despite 39,000 metres of historical drilling that failed to unlock the system, the new conceptual framework opens three distinct follow-up areas: a deeper high-grade target, a shallow bulk-tonnage zone, and a continuous hanging-wall vein system.

headline: DOUBLEVIEW OPENS FAR EAST ZONE — 8m at 4.04 g/t Au Extends BC Copper-Gold 150m Beyond PEA Pit Shell
snippet: Doubleview Gold Corp. (TSX-V: DBG) released June 9 assay results from seven drill holes (H102–H108) completed at its Hat copper-gold porphyry project in northwestern British Columbia, confirming gold-enriched mineralization approximately 150 metres east of the known resource envelope and naming the area the Far East Zone — highlighted by 8.0 metres grading 4.04 g/t Au and a broader 112.0-metre interval at 0.40 g/t Au. The results post-date both the February 2026 MRE and the March 2026 PEA, meaning the Far East Zone represents resource upside not yet captured in the market-facing economic study.

headline: SIRIOS LAUNCHES 25,000m AT CHEECHOO — Two Rigs on Ground in Quebec; Resource Update Feeds 2027 PEA
snippet: Sirios Resources Inc. (TSX-V: SOI) confirmed June 9 the commencement of Phase 1 drilling at its Cheechoo Gold Project in Eeyou Istchee, Quebec — the company's largest-ever program at 25,000 metres across two rigs, with a third rig arriving by end of June. The program targets three sectors: ~15,000 metres on the main exploration target, ~7,500 metres in the metasediment contact zone, and ~2,500 metres in the higher-grade Eclipse sector; a LIBS (Laser-Induced Breakdown Spectroscopy) unit is deployed on-site for real-time core characterization. Results feed an updated resource estimate that is required before a Preliminary Economic Assessment planned for H1 2027.

headline: CRITICAL ELEMENTS STARTS 10,000m ROSE WEST DRILL — Lithium Pegmatites Expanding in Quebec's Eeyou Istchee
source_name: Junior Mining Network / Critical Elements Lithium
snippet: Critical Elements Lithium Corp. (TSX-V: CRE) announced June 9 the start of its 10,000-metre summer drill program at the Rose West Discovery within its Rose Lithium-Tantalum Project in Quebec — one of the most advanced hardrock lithium projects in North America, backed by a completed Feasibility Study, C$150 million conditional financing, and Cree Nation neighbour agreements. The Winter 2026 program immediately preceding this campaign expanded the lateral footprint of mineralised pegmatites and identified new lithium-tantalum zones in both the hanging wall and footwall of the main Pegmatite 3, setting up the summer program to generate data for an updated resource estimate supporting a future permitting and financing push.

headline: LAHONTAN FINDS SLAB WEST — Unmapped Nevada Gold Zone Discovered Outside Existing Santa Fe Mine Resource
snippet: Lahontan Gold Corp. (TSX-V: LG) released June 9 its first 2026 drill results from the Santa Fe Mine Project in Churchill County, Nevada, including a discovery: five RC holes (1,530 metres) at the Slab West target — completely separate from the existing Slab open-pit resource — confirmed a previously unrecognized gold zone that remains open in all directions. A companion set of four diamond core holes (953 metres) at the Calvada deposit intercepted 90.8 metres grading 0.44 g/t Au Eq below the current resource pit shell; management notes this is the first true exploration drilling ever conducted at Santa Fe, making Slab West a genuinely new open-ended target on a project already hosting a 2+ million ounce resource.

headline: SUN PEAK SPUDS SAUDI VMS — 16.35 g/t Au Surface Gossan Targeted in Maiden 2,500m Halahila Drill
source_name: Junior Mining Network / Sun Peak Metals
snippet: Sun Peak Metals Corp. (TSX-V: PEAK) announced June 8 the commencement of its maiden diamond drill program at the Halahila Gold-Copper VMS Project in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia — the company's second drill campaign in Saudi Arabia in 2026, following completed drilling at its adjacent Safra VMS Project. The ~2,500-metre program targets the Halahila Main Zone, where a 650-metre-long mineralized gossan up to 30 metres wide has yielded surface samples of up to 16.35 g/t gold and 180 g/t silver; Sun Peak holds 13 exploration licences totalling 1,072 km² along VMS and gold trends in Saudi Arabia and Ethiopia, one of the broadest Arabian Peninsula exploration portfolios among TSX-V juniors.

headline: GOLD ETF MONEY WALKED IN MAY — Europe the Only Buyer; AUM Slips to $604bn as Rate Fears Sideline Western Capital
snippet: Gold ETF flows turned modestly negative in May 2026 — the first net-outflow month since early 2025 — as rangebound prices and renewed appetite for risk assets kept Western investors sidelined, with Europe the only region recording net inflows, per World Gold Council data reported June 7-8. Global gold-backed ETF AUM slipped 2% month-over-month to $604 billion while holdings eased to 4,121 tonnes, just below February's record high; the reversal in retail and institutional ETF demand is notable because it occurred while central bank buying remained structurally active — creating a bifurcated market where paper-market conviction waned just as hard-money accumulation continued.

headline: MP vs USA RARE EARTH — Motley Fool: Operating Mountain Pass Beats CHIPS Act Build-Out in June Risk-Reward
snippet: A June 8 Motley Fool analysis pits the two U.S. government-backed rare earth stocks head-to-head: MP Materials (NYSE: MP), which runs the only large-scale domestic REE mine at Mountain Pass and posted record Q1 NdPr output of 917 metric tons (up 63% year-over-year, sales up 117%), versus USA Rare Earth (USAR), which secured a $1.6 billion CHIPS Act deal in January to construct a complete mine-to-magnet supply chain but has no operating assets yet. The piece concludes MP is the better near-term buy given Pentagon equity stake, Apple and GM supply contracts, and government price floors — while acknowledging USAR's larger strategic upside if it successfully executes the 'Project Vault' mine-to-magnet thesis that targets China's refining monopoly.
